## 📋 How to Report Memory Issues in Zen

To help us investigate memory-related issues effectively, please follow these steps carefully:

### 1. Gather Troubleshooting Information

1. Open Zen and go to: [`about:support`](https://support.mozilla.org/kb/use-troubleshooting-information-page-fix-firefox)  
2. Click **"Copy text to clipboard"**  
3. Paste the copied text into the template

### 2. Capture Memory Report

1. Open a new tab and go to: `about:memory`  
2. Click the **"Measure and save…"** button  
3. With the downloaded file, drag and drop it into the template

### 3. Submit Your Report

In your comment under this issue, include both reports using the template below:


````
<Describe a bit your situation and whats wrong. Maybe also include a https://profiler.firefox.com/ if necessary>

<details>
<summary>About Support</summary>

```
REPLACE WITH ABOUT:SUPPORT CONTENTS
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>About memory</summary>

REPLACE WITH ABOUT:MEMORY FILE UPLOAD
</details>
````

## Before You Submit

- **Stay on topic.** Please keep this thread focused on memory issue reports only.
- **Use a clean testing environment.** Disable all **addons, custom themes, and mods** (`about:addons`) — these are known to affect performance.

## Optional: Test on the Latest Twilight Build

To help determine if your memory issue has already been addressed in recent changes, please try reproducing the problem using the **latest Twilight build**:

🔗 [Download Twilight build](https://zen-browser.app/download/?twilight)

## Comment 2997719150

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-06-23T19:34:41Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-2997719150


| user       | tabs† | Resident unique* (MB) | Machine / OS / Zen version                                   | notes|
| ---------- | ----------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -- |
| cmvalma    | 142         | 4917                  | Macbook air M1 16GB / macOS 15.5.0 / 1.12.10b                |  |
| rvsmooth   | 3           | 891                   | Intel Ivy Bridge (2012) 8GB/ Arch Linux 6.15.2 (X11) / 1.14t |  |
| Illustar0  | 19          | 8622                  | 32GB /Windows 11/1.13.1b                                     |  1 |
| Beeditor04 | 17          | 4450                  | Intel Laptop 16GB / Windows 11/ 1.13.2b                      |  |
| Beeditor04 |  4            | 7184                 | "                                                                                   | 2 |
| muhmudrik  | 17          | 852                   | Macbook Pro M1 8GB / macOS 15.5.0 / 1.13.2b                  | |
| Loolybooly | 10          | 2391                  | 32GB / Windows 11 / 1.13.2b                                  | |
| MW-J97     | 19          | 3155                  | 32GB / Fedora 42 Linux 6.14.11 (X11)                         | | 
| rubiin | 23 | 1780 | AMD 16GB / Arch Linux 6.15.3 (X11) / 1.13.2b | |
| abb4-r053  | 72          | 1771                  | 32GB Windows 11 / 1.13.2b                                    |3|

*I summed the processes 'resident-unique' values. In Windows this is called the active private working set: the amount of physical memory in use by the process that can't be used by other processes. This is also the value shown in task manager. 
This value is also know as the Unique Set Size (USS).
†These can include pinned/essential tabs that are not loaded after startup, but their tab objects exist and are prepared to be loaded. These not-yet-loaded pins consume ~10MB a piece. Explicitly unloaded tabs are completely 'destroyed' and consume ~0MB.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff98c5a-d9f1-428e-b7c8-86da3d5127ea)

I did not make totals of measures like 'resident-phys-footprint' (Mac's default memory shown per process) or 'resident' (resident set size (RSS) / working set: the amount of physical memory currently mapped by a process), because adding these values up would double-count shared memory. 
You can see remarks about this in Mozilla's own [memory telemetry code](https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/integration/autoland/file/tip/xpcom/base/MemoryTelemetry.cpp#l496) and a [detailed explanation](https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-platform/c/WGNOtjHdsdA) in a post on choices made in MacOS memory usage telemetry.

All in all I do not find these reports show unreasonable high memory usage. 

Notes:
1. @Illustar0 's figure looks high to me. According to the report most of it was caused by 4 GitHub pages (2 Copilot) using 3.8GB in total. 
2. 3.7GB of the memory use belonged to the GPU process. From the support info it shows the UHD integrated (CPU) graphics are active and not the dedicated nvidia RTX 3050 GPU, which explains why quite some shared system RAM is used as GPU memory.  
3. A relatively large portion of the main process's memory usage (and events) can be attributed to the DevTools.  Its orphan DOM nodes and JavaScript running in it; 500MB.

## Comment 3002044712

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-06-24T22:19:52Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3002044712

@Beeditor04  On startup pins/essentials show in `about:processes` even while not opened. They already get created empty but ready to go. In the process manager you see they're assigned some 34MB. This is mostly unmapped memory though. Actually active memory (resident unique) is around 10MB. Once they actually load this'll typically increase to 150MB or more.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f524ad67-a797-4458-98b4-602e3a50d66a)

In Firefox all pinned tabs get loaded by default instead of on demand, but if you change that preference flag to true (`browser.sessionstore.restore_pinned_tabs_on_demand`, defaults false in FF , true in Zen) you see the same behaviour. I guess creating the tab/window up front in an empty state is done for speed. 

3.7GB of your Zen's memory usage came from the GPU process. The support info shows your iGPU (UHD graphics) on the CPU was active and not your dGPU RTX 3050. This explains why quite some system RAM was used as Shared GPU memory.

## Comment 3037260240

other (NONE) · ozer85 · 2025-07-04T21:22:41Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3037260240

Apologies this isn't in the requested format because Zen actually crashed before I could output the details, but wanted to report as performance has dropped off a cliff for me since I updated to 1.14.1b this morning. Yesterday I was delighted with Zen and telling everyone how they should adopt it, today the browser is completely unusable - it slows to a crawl once it's been open for more than 15 minutes and eventually dies completely. I've not got more than 8 active tabs open and none of them are very intensive. Here is the relevant section from. the Apple crash report (I'm running a M4 Pro Mac mini with 24gb RAM and have disabled all the extensions and add ons as suggested):

## Comment 3265406978

other (NONE) · hampoelz · 2025-09-08T09:29:01Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3265406978

> Has the dev team looked into the fact that this might be an upstream issue? I am having the same issues with [LibreWolf](https://librewolf.net/), a firefox derivative.

> This usually happens when I let the browser open for long periods of time, even when not using. (I never turn off the computer)
> So it starts adding up RAM usage

Before switching to Zen, I used “stock” Firefox and had similar issues back then. When Firefox was open for a long period of time (several weeks/months) without restarting (which I don't think is unusual on a MacBook), it started to consume enormous amounts of RAM (10+ out of 16 GB on my system) and became slow and almost froze. So maybe part of the problem actually has to do with upstream Firefox?

When I switched to Zen, I was concerned that I would also have these memory and performance issues due to the Firefox base. And here we are. But surprisingly, I feel that the memory situation is better in Zen, but after a while, it also becomes slower and sluggish.

I will definitely keep an eye on it.

<details>
<summary>* why resident unique and not physical footprint</summary>
I summed the processes 'resident-unique' values. In Windows this is called the active private working set: the amount of physical memory in use by the process that can't be used by other processes. This is also the value shown in task manager.
This value is also know as the Unique Set Size (USS).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff98c5a-d9f1-428e-b7c8-86da3d5127ea)

I did not make totals of measures like 'resident-phys-footprint' (Mac's default memory shown per process) or 'resident' (resident set size (RSS) / working set: the amount of physical memory currently mapped by a process), because adding these values up would double-count shared memory.
You can see remarks about this in Mozilla's own [memory telemetry code](https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/integration/autoland/file/tip/xpcom/base/MemoryTelemetry.cpp#l496) and a [detailed explanation](https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-platform/c/WGNOtjHdsdA) in a post on choices made in MacOS memory usage telemetry.
</details>
<details>
<summary>† about pinned tabs</summary>
These can include pinned/essential tabs that are not loaded after startup, but their tab objects exist and are prepared to be loaded. These not-yet-loaded pins consume ~10MB a piece. Explicitly unloaded tabs are completely 'destroyed' and consume ~0MB.
</details>

Only some of these look problematic to me. Especially the case of @Holly-Chan where we see a clear case of a memory leak in the GPU-process taking up 10GB and even reporting 34GB private mem. Advise here, and to a few others; update your GPU drivers.
Another case, that of @constantinemagnus, has very high memory usage by 1 extension _MetaMask_. The reviews for that extension are full of complaints about mem usage/instability. You have also tweaked advanced configs to not cache to disk and keep more cache in memory + read ahead more video (x10 from the default), which of course increases memory use.

## Comment 3298863551

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-09-16T13:48:27Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3298863551

@enp-aszuszkiewicz  
Wow, that looks like another clear leak in the GPU process.

<img width="995" height="625" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/182b1e6c-45f8-415f-bdc4-8abb5fe07783" />

At the time of measuring I see only 1 tab open: Github. Did you have other tabs open at the time this memory use grew so high?
Any hint to what kind of activity / site might have triggered this? (e.g. browsing AliExpress, watching video / streaming)

## Comment 3312694994

other (NONE) · hampoelz · 2025-09-19T15:43:04Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3312694994

> Before switching to Zen, I used “stock” Firefox and had similar issues back then. When Firefox was open for a long period of time (several weeks/months) without restarting (which I don't think is unusual on a MacBook), it started to consume enormous amounts of RAM (10+ out of 16 GB on my system) and became slow and almost froze. So maybe part of the problem actually has to do with upstream Firefox?
> 
> I will definitely keep an eye on it.

For testing, I had two tabs open: GitHub and a SPA I'm currently working on, which reloads on every code change and has DevTools running alongside it. I've been leaving Zen minimised in the background over the last few days. The Activity Monitor now shows that almost 6 GB of memory are used by Zen. The memory report shows over 3 GB of total resident memory. However, I've noticed that it fluctuates a lot when I do multiple measurements (ranging from 2 to 4 GB). I'm not sure if this is intentional. To me, the report looks like a memleak in DevTools, as it consumes over 2 GB and is trending upwards. _(Once, it even consumed about 5 GB, but unfortunately I didn't save the report.)_

It seems that there is also an upstream bug report for this, but it has not been fixed since 6 years (!): https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1595797

Looks like there are several different memory leaks? A quick search on Bugzilla for memory leaks lists about 200 unresolved reported defects, which I think underlines this unfortunately.

## Comment 3403204589

other (NONE) · Redex68 · 2025-10-14T19:02:09Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3403204589

I'll repeat what I said in my separate issue here so it's in one place:

Zen seems to leave thousands (I've counted 1499 zen.exe instances running at one point using RAMMap) of processes with remaining kernel memory allocation, and presumably also some corresponding services. Using a large amount of memory and slowing down my system. These processes don't show up in Task Manager, only when using RAMMap.

Turning off extensions doesn't seem to affect the behaviour. I am unsure what all of the exact actions that cause more processes to spawn are, but from testing I've concluded that: opening new tabs (or clicking on unloaded tabs) adds multiple processes to the list, following links in the same tab doesn't seem to create new processes, sometimes a new process appears when doing either nothing or actions that previously didn't spawn a new process, unsure why that is. It also seems that the process count increases over time, but I'm not 100% sure, I'm guessing these processes are all just regular stuff for a browser, just that they aren't getting cleaned up propperly.

Notably I have to highlight that the number of processes I can see in RAMMap never decreases, not even when closing Zen, the number keeps increasing untill a full system restart, meaning that when I'm using my PC over the day, if I try to game at the end of the day it becomes unplayable because I have no RAM left.

Here are the numbers I got from some testing:
win startup -> 0 zen.exe instances found in RAMMap output
zen launched -> 15
3 tabs opened -> 22
zen closed -> 22
reopened -> 34
another tab opened -> 42
closed zen after waiting some time -> 42
reopened and played a video -> 66

test 2:
open -> 16
reopen -> 24
time passed -> 24
open yt -> 28
watch for 2 mins -> 28
jump around links within youtube -> 28
close zen -> 28
clicked some unloaded tabs, opened new ones -> 85
open Wikipedia -> 90
following links within wikipedia -> 90
opening new website by following link on wikipedia (same tab) -> 91
going back 10 times -> 91

In testing I wasn't able to easily get to a thousand processes, I'm not sure if something special happened the times I got to that high a number or whether I was just using my browser a lot, but I've experienced severe memory usage problems multiple times over the past month, causing frame drops in games from lack of available RAM.

Since I had originally posted the issue, I have once again had it jump up to 544 processes in RAMMap just by regular everyday use. This session is the one I've provided the troubleshooting and memory information for, but from a quick glance at it, I don't think it's visible in the memory report, as I don't think it's something Zen/Firefox is able to track.

Here's a screenshot form RAMMap from when I had 1499 zen.exe instances, you can see that the Page Table is using 7.6 GB which is highly unusual:
<img width="1174" height="503" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ca6d2dd-bb8f-499b-b17d-f04a2ab7fb84" />

Here's what one of those entries looks like:
<img width="871" height="187" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd87caed-7f64-42e5-8c36-b263f367a6b8" />

@Redex68 Looks like you discovered a case of zombie processes; Processes where all threads are closed, but the process itself is not.
The mem usage is in "Standby" which is like a cache where previous items are not thrown out of memory yet for faster performance if needed again. This is low priority and gets evicted easily when another process really needs the space.
It's therefore also not counted towards memory usage when looking at tools like task manager. (it's called "cached" in the performance > memory tab) 

I can recreate this, but not in the thousands. As a result also not with such a large page table size. When closing Zen I regularly get 1 or 2 new zombies from the main and GPU processes. 
Have you been able to correlate the process IDs with the process description in Zen's process manager?

## Comment 3410860570

other (NONE) · Redex68 · 2025-10-16T13:19:01Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3410860570

> This is low priority and gets evicted easily when another process really needs the space.
It's therefore also not counted towards memory usage when looking at tools like task manager.

The problem is it doesn't seem to get evicted, my system runs out of memory and things start lagging whilst this is still taking up memory, and you can actually also see it in task manager, task manager would say the system is using 31/32 GB, and most of it isn't in standby, it explicitly says it's "in use", just that when you look at the processes tab the processes there wouldn't add up to that total.

> Have you been able to correlate the process IDs with the process description in Zen's process manager?

I'm not sure how to do this? Each process has a different ID, so I'm not sure how I'd connect them to their original purpose when there are hundreds. E.g. right now, after using my PC for about 4 hours, I have 530 zen.exe processes in RAMMap. I also noticed I have e.g. 5341 svchost.exe, 5180 netsh.exe, and 5450 conhost.exe instances in RAMMap right now. Do you know if that's normal? I'm assuming these are probably also leftovers from Zen, which would make sense since even 1500 zen.exe instances taking up 36kb each shouldn't be enough to fill up 32 gigs of RAM.

## Comment 3446547902

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-10-25T10:39:56Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3446547902

@dezren39 This file has an unexpected end of file and is corrupt.

<img width="610" height="521" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90e6b664-87aa-4e98-be50-732bc70a72d6" />

Repairing the end (unknown how many entries we miss) allowed opening it.
Looking at it does point to the culprit: Youtube. 

<img width="1056" height="826" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f543ea28-0a2a-4cb2-a45b-74ff97117562" />

From the report it seems there were 4x9 = 36 media blobs (videos) in memory. With so many video tabs open I'm not surprised a lot of memory is used. 

At the time of the report both "Session Buddy" and "Tab Session Manager" were active. That feels double and I'm unsure how well they work in Zen with its altered tab / folder handling. The Session Buddy extension on Firefox is not from the real author of the Chrome extension. Rather dodgy. 
The Tab session manager extension's reviews also don't look too positive on Firefox:

<img width="799" height="92" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d053dbc9-f190-4d4e-bc76-fc1fcc27896d" />

I'd advise removing them both and going easy on the number of Youtube tabs you open and/or pin (in folders?).

## Comment 3467447733

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-10-30T11:14:35Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3467447733

@zhuxining There've been several issue with macOS 26 (Tahoe) betas and Firefox 144. A couple of examples:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1982717
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1943005
A new FF release 144.0.2  tries to fix some, mainly QoS related issues. So hopefully the next Zen release based on this would improve things for macOS 26 users.

## Comment 3604176832

reporter (MEMBER) · mr-cheffy · 2025-12-02T22:12:04Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3604176832

> Doubt it makes a difference since this thread is from Jun 8 and this is still a problem, either that or other legitimate issues are just being rolled into here instead of being researched.

@Rydsmith There isn't a single root cause here. People are reporting a variety of symptoms, and they're all getting grouped together. Some cases are real memory leaks, others are just normal spikes caused by heavy workloads, and some are probably unrelated bugs that only appear similar on the surface. The point is: there's no universal "Zen is slow" or "Zen uses too much RAM" problem. There are many environmental factors and user mistakes involved, and it's not as simple as "just fix it".

This is a `[meta]` issue, as the title indicates. It's a place where reports can be collected, and when we have time, we look through them for actual anomalies. Most of them boil down to users installing lots of mods, add-ons, themes, and so on, without realizing the performance impact these can have on the browser. That's not necessarily a Zen issue; in general, the more you install, the slower things get.

This issue likely won't ever be closed or resolved, because it isn't meant to address one specific bug. If a genuine, reproducible issue is found, a separate report will be created for proper investigation and fixing.

That said, giving a bit more of background, explanations, about:processes, etc when commenting or even posting a profiler report (https://profiler.firefox.com/) would help even more as just giving out an about:memory is as useful as just showing a screenshot of the task manager (not very useful).

## Comment 3611177013

other (NONE) · RetroitKnife · 2025-12-04T09:51:50Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3611177013

I have been sort of plagued by a memory leak (I think?) as well. However reproducing it is really difficult, because it happens only sometimes and additionally only after having Zen open for a really long time, like +5hrs (with usually my device going to sleep in between). When it happens I can see Zen using 20GB minimum, which is quite alot but I guess that's because I have many tabs open at the same time. But then, to make matters worse, when I close Zen to free the memory _sometimes_ it would stay open in background and just start eating memory, like it gains memory each few seconds one more GB and I have to kill it via command.

I do wonder though if this could be caused by my extensions, however I did not have these problems with the same extensions in Floorp (which in general I feel like used less memory, I could be wrong though).

The memory report below is after I reopened Zen.

## Comment 3679071853

other (NONE) · ghost · 2025-12-21T16:26:17Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3679071853

So, I may have found one of the root causes for the high memory uses.

It has something to do with Enhanced Tracking Protection.

LibreWolf uses a modified "Custom" preset, so I wondered if I could use the same protection preset in Zen too, low and behold, setting the preset to "Custom" causes a drop in memory usage from 1.2GB to 900MB+

Before:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eff946b-3694-47a7-a6ae-4350ce571923) 

After:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e67bcfdb-21f8-4965-9db7-9228f6f9ce82)

## Comment 3679324636

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2025-12-21T19:37:38Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3679324636

@MyNamesTee Just know that by doing this you disable Total Cookie Protection and third party cookies are no longer isolated (or blocked). This means some services / sites (e.g. facebook, Google) can track your activity across different sites on the internet.

Containerisation of cookies and data to limit its use to 1 site/domain does lead to duplication and thus increases the memory required. This is the price you pay for security and privacy.

## Comment 3709622028

other (NONE) · not-varram · 2026-01-05T09:33:20Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3709622028

@RetroitKnife @Sahityaaryan  Wanted to let you know you're not alone in this. To follow up; I have a system with almost 64 gigs of ram. And quite simply having zen open over the course of 9 hours (again no major change in total # of tabs open) causes zen to take up nearly all of my system's ram. (slowy creeps from 10 gigs of usage)

I feel we are all facing the same type of issue/maybe memory leak??

I have the exact same arch setup on windows (which I use w/ way more tabs (like in the thousands)) and ram is quite simply a non-issue there); so issue seems to be with arch/Linux specifically?

At this point i am fairly confident it is a memory leak issue, because no way zen is using almost 40 gigs of ram with only ~200 tabs open.  (P.S. this is after ~ 9hours of usage w/ the same amount of tabs open; Ram usage goes from like 4-10 gigs to 40...)

I noticed my report was mentioned here so wanted to add a bit of context :) #11721 ; Please let me know if I can add or give anything extra to help resolve this.

## Comment 3809580132

other (NONE) · AwesomesuperDan0927 · 2026-01-28T07:48:40Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3809580132

Hi, I've been using Zen Browser for a while now, and its been the best browser that I have used so far. In the past I've experienced high RAM usage with zen on my Mac, causing system alerts about memory overload occasionally, but I was told that its a common issue so I didn't really bother much as I only needed to restart the browser. However, ever since v1.18.2b which I updated just an hour ago, I have had to quit and reopen zen more than half a dozen times due to excessive RAM usage slowing down my computer. Really appreciate what you guys are doing, and hope that there is a fix to this soon. Thanks!

## Comment 3835430673

other (NONE) · Matteoverzotti · 2026-02-02T14:21:51Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3835430673

Hi, I've been using Zen for maybe half a year now and it's never been worse on mac in terms of energy. Having a few tabs open consumes more energy than my heavy docker containers. Before I had to quit it (Cmd + Q) maybe once a week due to it becoming laggy (I supposed memory leaks). Now I have to do that at least once a day because it would simply stop working and overheat my laptop. I attached a screenshot below with the energy consumption from task manager and `about:support` and `about:memory` as you asked. 

Thank you for such a great browser, but I'll have to switch momentarily as my macbook pro doesn't last more than 2 hours with Zen open.

## Comment 3900372090

other (NONE) · RetroitKnife · 2026-02-14T01:15:42Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-3900372090

So I made a new discovery today.

[This Website](https://de.elegoo.com/products/galaxy-pla-filament-1-75mm-colored-1kg) (store for buying 3D printing stuff) is single-handedly able to use >10GB RAM for one single tab. The only thing you need to do is click a bit through it, look at some items, scroll through some images.

I do have some privacy addons that I'll list below, but honestly, there is no way that this should happen in any case. During normal usage a tab never goes above 200MB of RAM.

I also found out that with similar addons on Librewolf the same behavior can be observed. It is really specific to the Elegoo Website.

### Addons in Zen:
- AdNauseam
- ArchiveBox Exporter
- CanvasBlocker
- ClearURLs
- Decentraleyes
- Facebook Container
- Firefox Multi-Account Containers
- Gesturefy
- KeePassXC-Browser
- Plasma Integration
- Proton Pass: Free Password Manager
- Return YouTube Dislike
- YouTube NonStop

### Addons in Librewolf:
- CanvasBlocker
- ClearURLs
- Decentraleyes
- Return YouTube Dislike
- uBlock Origin

> Note: CanvasBlocker configured with "Stealth" preset.

The thing is, it wasn't always like that. With the same setup and browser I could browser the website normally, so something must've changed somewhat recently. I am pretty sure this is not a Zen specific issue and probably a more broad Firefox problem, but I think it is still worth mentioning.

I have made some screen recordings and profiling-data but they contain sensitive data and are also quite big. If any dev is interested in them please contact me privately.

Would be cool if somebody would try to reproduce this, I wonder if this is specific to my setup.

## Comment 4106761419

reporter (MEMBER) · mr-cheffy · 2026-03-22T18:41:42Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4106761419

Cool thing I found by the way:

These common transparency themes often add `will-change: transform` to the browser view which will affect negatively your performance exponentially.

These are my results:

without: https://share.firefox.dev/4spRgnI

<img width="1778" height="286" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd34ef30-0450-469e-aa7a-daf428cd74ba" />

with: https://share.firefox.dev/4uKp8gF

<img width="2118" height="306" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5014e9b3-d43a-482c-9240-c6053ac43b21" />

so please do check your themes if you are having similar issues.

## Comment 4160503053

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-03-31T07:25:08Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4160503053

> I also found out that with similar addons on Librewolf the same behavior can be observed. It is really specific to the Elegoo Website.

@RetroitKnife 
Not able to reproduce the issue on that website. It could be related to your addons.

Try without the ClearURLs addon. Reading its reviews several report it breaks certain websites and in the past also caused a lot of reloads > increased RAM. (its functionality can mostly be replaced by a [filter](https://github.com/uBlockOrigin/uAssets/blob/master/filters/privacy-removeparam.txt) you can add to uBlock origin or AdNauseam)

Also Firefox's enhanced tracking protection (ETP) when set to strict mode will strip [some URL trackers](https://firefox.settings.services.mozilla.com/v1/buckets/main/collections/query-stripping/records) already.

## Comment 4412781093

other (NONE) · zehawki · 2026-05-09T14:44:59Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4412781093

Here's some data, if it helps:

I use FF, Opera, Vivaldi, Brave continuously and simultaneously with lots of tabs open in each. For a new context, I need a fresh browser, so after hunting around chanced upon Zen.

Fresh Zen installation (Win 11, 32GB memory, Intel Ultra 5) with no extensions - 4 tabs open and it hit 3.7GB which seemed excessive, so I started hunting around and found this issue. 

However, subsequently it has reduced to 2.3GB. To cross check I opened the same in Brave (which already has many tabs open). Here's a tab by tab snapshot comparison:

| Tab                    | Brave | Zen  |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ---- |
| Stripe                  | 631   | 703  |
| 2 google workspace tabs | 870   | 950  |
| Zoho desk               | 218   | 230  |
|                         | 1719  | 1883 |

Seems to be by and large the same.

As a separate datapoint, Windows reports 2.3GB for Zen, and 1.9GB for Brave (with these 4 tabs + a dozen more)

## Comment 4495005360

other (NONE) · igads3d · 2026-05-20T06:00:56Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4495005360

The memory leak issue is really annoying. It's fine for a day or two, or three, but at some point it just baloons until there is no free RAM left. I had to restart the PC a few times because zen hogged it all, OOMKiller didn't do anything about it (that may be a skill issue on my part), and I failed to kill zen in time before the computer stopped responding completely. 

I spent some time in troubleshoot mode, didn't touch any settings, and memory leak still seems to be present.
 
I started at about 4 gb and after 1.5 days RAM usage increased to 9gb, at which point i stopped the experiment. During that time I mostly just watched YT and did a few searches.

_Interesting observation:_ RAM usage didn't grow linearly. For a day it was staying at stable 5-6gb, next day it was the same for hours. And then I open 4 tabs and usage rises to 9gb. After restarting and reopening the same tabs, ram didn't grow to the same 9gb and stayed at about 5-7gb.

The tab count was about 30ish, of them about 8-15 were active, depending on my YT queue and active searches.

I didn't test zen to complete failure, until it hogs all the free RAM I have, because it was too painful to use without an adblocker and on default settings(disabled hw acceleration), especially for a few days, but I still don't think this is normal for a browser to use 9gb of RAM for that much tabs. I was using firefox with the same set of extensions until approximately a year ago and it didn't do that.

Another interesting observation: when I was saving a memory report, i saw 9gb used by zen in Resources app. about:memory, however, reported only about 4.3gb of total resident memory. 
Not sure, how Resources counts application (not process) memory, but it seems legit to me, because when it reported zen using 12+gb of RAM and close to 100% overall memory (I have 16gb), it strongly correlated to my computer hanging entirely.

## Comment 4498403196

other (NONE) · igads3d · 2026-05-20T12:30:48Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4498403196

> Your 6GB memory report only shows 2GB? Maybe its just showing up reserved memory which shouldn't be an issue as it should get freed if the OS needs it

In that case the computer wouldn't stop responding when memory is reported at 12+gb.
I did some research, the value Resources gives me is very close to a sum of RSS values of all zen processes. Memory report shows a value close to sum of PSS values. 
That's probably the cause of the discrepancy.

If I'm correct here, that would mean that the issue may lie somewhere in the shared memory or some shared libs

## Comment 4499420815

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-05-20T14:30:26Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4499420815

## Comment 4789682108

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-06-24T13:16:08Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4789682108

@Subham-chaudhary 
> Adding to what's already being discussed here

I'm going to be blunt. This is not adding anything useful to the discussion and you pinged over 65 participants. It's even unclear which site you were watching that video on. With the info you've shared it's not possible to tell if it was an issue with the browser itself, a particular website or maybe an extension.
The task manager is a pretty terrible source of info because it mostly just shows "Zen" processes.
A better clue what the problematic process/tab is comes from the internal process manager (SHIFT+ESC). If at all possible add an about:memory report next time. You also forgot to add a about:support report.

@Pendonym The uploaded report appears to be corrupt. The JSON stops in the middle of an array and is not properly closed (syntax error). 
I closed the end, but of course don't know how much is missing. With what we have now it's only showing ~800MB usage.

<img width="762" height="63" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0125a745-03ce-4df5-a30e-2a9d0fe9f5e2" />

Can you try making one again while the high RAM usage occurs & that can be loaded without syntax error when using the 'load...' button in about:memory?
In any case a good check would be testing without extensions enabled. Especially things like uBO or Violentmonkey blocking scripts can leads to a site doing spurious retries/loads. uBO has [a logger](https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/wiki/The-logger) you can use to check if this is happening but the "blocked on this page" \#  quickly going into tens of thousands can be an easy first tell . Auto-fill features of password managers like Proton can also cause (performance) issues because they parse/filter trough all the page elements (every chat message too) searching for credential fields to hook into/popup. 


## Comment 4789894689

other (NONE) · Subham-chaudhary · 2026-06-24T13:40:47Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4789894689

@Propheticus 
> The task manager is a pretty terrible source of info because it mostly just shows "Zen" processes.

Yea you're right about that, but as i said ***Zen wasn't responding at all***
And the only thing I could do is to open the Task Manager, nothing else.

> It's even unclear which site you were watching that video on.

Well you can see the 4th process in the process tree, which is responsible for handling the current open tab, 
and there's nothing wrong with that its jus `247.5 MB` which seems pretty reasonable for a streaming site. `animetsu.cc`

The main culprit here is the first two tabs consuming `5365.7 MB` and `2771.7 MB` memory.
First sub-process seems to be the main process of the zen browser and the next process could be any of the following.
- Shared Web Process
- GPU
- Extension

> If at all possible add an about:memory report next time. You also forgot to add a about:support report.

Due to unresponsive behavior, I couldn't do anything but `End the Process` using Task Mnager.

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-06-24T15:56:00Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-4791199019

@Subham-chaudhary  Still see no `about:support` (see the opening post!) ... It  would help us see what extensions you have. Maybe there's some known culprits amongst them. It also shows the GPU driver version and reports graphics failure reasons and important changes to the default config. 
Yes, those other processes could be GPU or Extension. With the info we have now we can only speculate though. 

Does this growing mem use happen 'on demand' when using the video website that is not named? Do you have any idea of another trigger? If yes, please use the profiler https://profiler.firefox.com/  to record a trace. Start a recording > trigger the growth > wait a few seconds (10 is plenty) > stop the recording and share (top-right button to upload+share). Hopefully that is possible before a full hang.

## Comment 5002058679

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-07-17T10:23:24Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5002058679

@shivanshs9 Is that memory report taken while seeing the high memory usage? I see only ~1.5GB resident unique usage. 

Please try the site with all extensions disabled. Especially Bitwarden (with autofill enabled) is a suspect. In the BW extension you can add AWS to 'blocked domains' to test. 

## Comment 5185517497

other (NONE) · rexendevar · 2026-08-04T22:56:04Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5185517497

Hi, I'm once again asking for any method of collecting useful information when Zen freezes. I've bound F1 to open the about:processes but again it does not work when Zen is frozen. I managed to open the page once while my fans were spinning up and I saw Zen itself (not extensions) taking well over 100% CPU but that;s the only info I have. I will do everything I can to help fix this problem, as it happens at least once every single day with no way of predicting it. But I need a consistent way to get data. 

## Comment 5354326290

other (NONE) · LucHeart · 2026-08-20T09:55:48Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5354326290

Hey, i have also noticed a lot of full browser freezes, two entirely different machines, both windows 11. Im not sure how to help debug this, collect any useful data on what stalls it. Sometimes I need to fully kill my zen to revive it, note that this already happens with less than 5-10 tabs open. I often only notice it due to my video playback pausing for a few seconds. It doesn't seem to be memory related from what i can tell.

## Comment 5355723394

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-08-20T12:14:01Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5355723394

@LucHeart There's been several of these reports, especially by users with an Nvidia GPU. I see similar reports for Firefox.
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2027413

What has helped a few users during troubleshooting so far is going into `about:config` and setting `gfx.webrender.compositor` to false + restarting. Worth a try until Firefox (and/or Nvidia) fixes what is causing the webrender issues.

## Comment 5619451661

other (NONE) · MaverickMartyn · 2026-09-10T13:27:59Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5619451661

Zen consistently gets slower and eats more and more RAM, in particular on YouTube.
I just had to kill a YouTube tab using over 9GB of RAM. For a SINGLE tab.
I had heard so many great things about Zen, hence why I've been trying it out for a few months, but this is making me consider switching again.  
My entire PC will grind to a halt because Zen is suddenly eating 12+ GB of memory. This is especially common when browsing YouTube shorts for extended sessions.
I already restarted it, but I'll try to post a detailed report next time it happens.

## Comment 5697954167

other (NONE) · codeforge11 · 2026-09-16T13:07:52Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5697954167

Zen's RAM usage is terrible. I've been using it for almost a year and I'm very happy with how it looks and feels, but when I have just 2 tabs open (YouTube and X), it takes 12GB of RAM. I've already tried restarting the browser and clearing the cache, but nothing helps. Please fix it because I don't want to switch to another browser.

## Comment 5705679700

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-09-16T22:52:17Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5705679700

@codeforge11 This is not actionable. Follow the request in the opening post to add information that helps us possibly spotting a cause; is it the GPU  process, an extension, the main process, some buggy Javascript on a site? We simply don't know from your complaint. 
12GB of RAM is clearly too much for 2 tabs, only that is clear.
It could be a leak, but I'm unable to trigger one on my machines.
Sadly Youtube is known to cause them on Firefox and its forks for some users.  Especially while scrolling **shorts** and for adblock users. 
Are you watching normal video's, doomscroll the shorts or perhaps watch a livestream?

## Comment 5709093579

other (NONE) · aki665 · 2026-09-17T05:13:13Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5709093579

After updating to 1.22.2b, youtube freezes and starts using massive amount of ram after interacting with the queue feature. 

At first, I had a tab from yesterday, which had had a queue with some videos. The queue was emptied by youtube (as it does sometimes. Sometimes the queue stays for days.), but the url still included the previous queues information (the query string that's something like `&list=<random letters and numbers>&index=<number>`). If I tried to add a video to the queue, the page froze and did the whole memory leak thing.

After trying that a couple of times, I tried to open a new tab of youtube and start a new queue. I can add videos to a queue, but if I try to open the next video in the queue, the freeze and memory leak happen.

Here's a performance profile of case 2: https://profiler.firefox.com/public/jtb3b4qbj8t0139fk5ccd3nhkm2k18q1x8j1vyg/calltree/?globalTrackOrder=0w2&thread=1&v=17

(might be unrelated, but that website's share popup is very slow)

## Comment 5722127182

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-09-17T22:34:40Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5722127182

@aki665 Before I look into the memory report further, already a few points from the support info

- You have the Wappalyzer extension installed and enabled. This has caused massive memory leaks in the past. Even if those are solved, it's known to slow down the browser a lot. Especially Youtube. Please test with the extensions disabled or removed.
- Your about:config  flags contains a value `gfx.blacklist.video-overlay.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID` . This compatibility check went wrong in Zen in the past due to us querying using the Zen version instead of the Firefox base version. It could be disabling this HW acceleration feature while there's no real reason to. Advise: go into about:config and delete this whole value. (this allows a new compat check against the Mozilla maintained blocklist do its thing. The result could still be a block of course, but then it's valid.)
- There's several YT related extensions active. If the 2 suggestions above didn't help, try disabling them all. (Especially  Reddit on youtube and isthereanydeal/Everywhere which have been abandoned and not had updates in years)

A first look at the performance profile shows it's in a loop updating the playlist. It appears to be trying to apply a shuffle:

<img width="523" height="609" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0e2adea-83c9-4d16-a916-dd014dba09fd" />

<img width="1113" height="227" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5901ac35-e789-4f4f-80d0-2a53523b83f4" />

It's using a lot of resources, memory continuously grows (leak) and starts triggering major garbage collection. Some other (network) processes are blocked and waiting for the main thread for over 1,5 minute.

<img width="759" height="263" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9f4f95b-e4c2-440c-b865-f484cf6c7a39" />

## Comment 5838370396

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-09-25T19:31:08Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5838370396

@emryll I can't tell which one due to anonymisation, but process 9936 was a website process with ~19GB of committed private memory (not necessarily mapped/used). Next time you encounter this you can use Ctrl+Esc to open Zen's process manager to see which tab/site it is.

@woories19 Did you update Zen to 1.22.3b before or after these issues started? And if it was after; anything else changed around the time the lagging started? 
From your about:config could you delete `gfx.blacklist.video-overlay.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID`
and set `gfx.webrender.dcomp-video-hw-overlay-win-force-enabled` back to its default value "false"?

## Comment 5973482637

other (NONE) · rexendevar · 2026-10-03T21:06:28Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5973482637

<img width="1235" height="223" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15058535-7f33-43e1-9718-821ca7c61e36" />
After killing Zen from system monitor. Note that when the memory leak happens, the memory usage grows over the course of maybe a minute, and I CANNOT do any kind of memory report at the time as the browser is effectively FROZEN. So the report attached is from afterwards. Please let me know what if anything I can do to capture any useful information on a frozen browser window for diagnostics. This has been happening nearly every single day I use Zen for months on end and I'm getting really seriously frustrated as I've seen no indication that it's even possible to figure out what's happening. This is not a simple case of Zen using more memory than it should, this is a fans-blasting freeze-crash which happens quite literally every single day - either while I'm using it, or in the middle of the damn night when my computer is locked and the screen is off. I'll be in bed and I hear my fans start to blast and I say god dammit Zen is crashing again.

## Comment 5994821764

other (NONE) · haasele · 2026-10-05T12:52:12Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-5994821764

I found one trigger of the current memory spikes, when I open a second instance of zen and immediately click on a new tab it spikes to around 40gb of RAM Usage, it normalizes after like 2min.The Browser is getting unresponive in that time, so i cant get diagnostics up and running. Happens reproducibly on GitHub pages (like the one here). I also noticed a major performance degration since the last update (Curerently running Version 1.22.3b) for GitHub Pages, could be linked.

I'm running on Linux, Kernel 7.2.7-1-cachyos - Zen got installed via System package as bin (yay -S zen-browser-bin). Reinstalling the browser didn't fix it.

My other Machine is running Zen via Flatpak, no issues there so far.

## Comment 6004362934

other (NONE) · Propheticus · 2026-10-05T22:23:13Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-6004362934

@michaelhazan  In your  case it looks like a Github actions tab has 5 'ghost' pages and is holding on to a lot of orphan (JS) objects that are not cleared from memory. Could the Refined Github extension be playing a role here?

@rexendevar There's some mentions of (webrender) features being on a blocklist for your iGPU / driver.  eg for reason "FEATURE_FAILURE_BROKEN_DRIVER". 
These blocklists exist to disable features that have known issues (like crashes, mem leaks, instability) on certain hardware/drivers/os or combinations of those. 
I see you ignored those by altering these preferences: 

```
gfx.webgpu.ignore-blocklist: true
gfx.webrender.all: true
```
And set all webrender features on forcefully.  
Advise: revert these 2 settings to their default.

also delete these entries so they can be re-evaluated:
```
gfx.blacklist.accelerated-canvas2d.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
gfx.blacklist.dmabuf.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
gfx.blacklist.gl.threadsafe.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
```


## Comment 6006827274

other (NONE) · emryll · 2026-10-06T00:47:28Z · https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/issues/8932#issuecomment-6006827274

@Propheticus I encountered the issue I reported 2 weeks ago for a second time, this time with total 28GB RAM usage. I looked at the process manager inside Zen and it turns out to be a chatgpt.com tab left open, taking up 22GB. I think it's likely that it was the same one causing high RAM usage last time.

I did not see this tab having such high memory usage earlier than just now, even though the tab has not been used in several hours. Zen (and this problem tab) has been running for >10h.
